name: Highlands 41

alpha.desc: The alpha view shows the front of the property from the street side, revealing a multi-wing single-story residence with flat and low-pitched roof sections situated in the upper-left portion of the parcel|A paved driveway curves from the front of the property and loops near the structure, providing a turnaround area|The remainder of the large parcel is open desert terrain with scattered native shrubs and trees across the undeveloped foreground|A paved road runs along the front perimeter of the property, providing direct street-level access.

bravo.desc: The bravo view shows the property from the right side, revealing the multi-section residence with a prominent solar panel array mounted on the darker roof section at the rear wing|A paved loop driveway is clearly visible wrapping around the front and side of the residence, with a gravel or compacted surface area adjacent to the structure providing vehicle staging space|Several mature trees cluster tightly around the structure on the right side, which may limit lateral access and visibility on that flank|The open desert terrain to the right and rear provides no significant vehicle barriers in those directions.

charlie.desc: The charlie view shows the rear of the property, with the residence positioned in the right portion of a very large open desert parcel|A small irrigated green lawn area is visible immediately adjacent to the rear of the residence, with dense tree clusters flanking the structure on both sides|The large open undeveloped area extending to the rear and left offers unobstructed overland approach from those directions|No visible fencing or walls enclose the rear perimeter of the parcel.

delta.desc: The delta view shows the property from the left side, with the residence and its dark-roofed garage or rear wing visible in the upper right of the frame|The left side of the parcel is entirely open desert with scattered juniper trees and low shrubs, with no fencing or structures obstructing movement along this flank|A paved road is visible along the lower-left edge of the parcel|The long, unobstructed open terrain on the left side provides ample staging and approach opportunities for emergency vehicles.

considerations: The residence is set well back from the street on a large open desert parcel, requiring a long approach via a single curved paved driveway. The loop driveway near the structure allows for vehicle turnaround without the need to reverse on the approach road. Dense tree clusters immediately surrounding the residence on multiple sides may limit close-access movement and ground-level visibility of exterior walls. The large undeveloped open terrain on the left and rear of the parcel provides alternative overland approach routes for emergency vehicles if needed.
clarifications: Does the driveway entrance from the street have any gate, barrier, or access control that would delay emergency vehicle entry? What is the surface material of the turnaround area adjacent to the residence — paved, gravel, or compacted dirt — and can it support the weight of heavy emergency apparatus? Are there any locked gates or fenced enclosures not visible from the aerial imagery that restrict perimeter access around the structure? Is the solar panel installation on the roof equipped with a rapid shutdown system, and where is the main electrical disconnect located?
